# context-verdict
One verdict for a whole session, before it is compacted.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]
context_verdict_build / context_verdict_judge is now available; Build a session snapshot, then ask f
or one verdict on whether compaction would lose unlanded state.
## The question, and the question this tool refuses
> **Is there unlanded state that a compaction would lose?**

That is a question about the *session*, not about any part of it. It has a
decidable answer: work ei
ther exists somewhere durable or it does not.

**This tool cannot tell you which parts of a context are important.** That was
tried. A per-block sc

reener — "which of these thirty blocks can be dropped?" — was
built and measured, and it failed in b
oth directions at once:
| what it judged | verdict | confidence |

| the block containing the actual fix | droppable | **0.323** |
| a nursery rhyme | worth keeping |

containing the actual fix | droppable | **0.323** |
| a nursery rhyme | worth keeping | **0.691** |

The most expensive possible error and pure noise, on the same data, in the same
run. So the capabili

ty is absent by construction rather than by policy — see
"Structural, not promised" below.
## The three verdicts
| verdict | meaning |

| `safe_to_compact` | nothing recorded is unlanded |
| `wait` | the record does not settle it, or th

e service could not be asked |
| `preserve_first` | recorded work exists nowhere durable and must be
written down first |

Exactly three, in that order, and there is no argument that adds a fourth. If you
are asked to drop

context, this is the wrong tool — say so, and use the three-value
answer instead.
## What counts as unlanded

The closed field set is read, rendered into the state, and **counted**. The count is
what the risk b

and compares against, so a field that is rendered but not counted
would be work the verdict cannot s

ee. All five unlanded fields count: unlanded
todos, changed-and-uncommitted files, unanswered questi

ons, unrecorded decisions,
and next steps. `session` and `risk_hints` are not items and are not coun

unrecorded decisions,
and next steps. `session` and `risk_hints` are not items and are not counted.
| field | counted as unlanded | why |

| `uncommitted` | yes | changed and not committed |
| `todos` | yes | not marked done in the session

's own record |
| `questions` | yes | asked and not answered |
| `decisions` | yes | made and not re

corded durably |
| `next_steps` | yes | planned and not landed |
| `risk_hints` | no | derived from

the counts above, not an item |
| `session` | no | identity, not work |

A session whose only unlanded work is recorded decisions is therefore **not**
`safe_to_compact`: the

count is above zero, so the local rules either decline into
`wait` or, past `waitMin`, answer `pres

ove zero, so the local rules either decline into
`wait` or, past `waitMin`, answer `preserve_first`.
## Structural, not promised

"We will not write that loop" is a promise, and the measurement above is what
happens when a promise

is all you have. Four gates, each with an executable
assertion, and the artefact check injects the
thing each one forbids:

**G1 — the model's input cannot name a block.** The state comes from exactly one
renderer over a clo

sed field set (`session`, `todos`, `uncommitted`, `questions`,
`decisions`, `next_steps`, `risk_hint

s`) and no field can express a block. `judge`
accepts only a state bound to its summary **by digest*

*, so a hand-assembled state
is refused rather than accepted on its word.

**G2 — three values plus one scale.** One `choice` question with exactly three
fixed options, plus o

ne `score`. A request with four options is refused; a
four-option request is injected in the artefac

e`. A request with four options is refused; a
four-option request is injected in the artefact check.

**G3 — no slot for a selection.** `FORBIDDEN_KEYS` is a constant of 35 names, and a
payload carrying

one **throws rather than being stripped**. Stripping would return a
plausible verdict while hiding

that something upstream produces the forbidden
shape. The refusal names the path (`$.outer.inner[0].

perBlock`) and cites the
measurement.
**G4 — no per-block API surface.** Three tools. No `screen`, no `filter`, no `pick`.
## What `wait` means
`wait` is the answer in three situations, and none is a bug:

1. the recorded unlanded count is ambiguous — inside the band between `safeMax` and
`waitMin` — so t
was asked and was not there.

The reason codes say which. In all three the answer is **not** permission: this
tool never treats "I

could not decide" as "go ahead". The local path decides the
two ends — nothing unlanded, or more th

an the threshold — and does not spend a
request on either.
## Exit codes
| code | meaning |

| `0` | no `lost` case was let through |
| `1` | a `lost` case **was** judged `safe_to_compact` |
|

`2` | the state exceeded its character budget — a configuration problem, not a verdict |
| `3` | usa
ge, configuration or input error |

A run where the service was absent is exit **0** with every case counted as SKIP.
That is deliberate

and it is the one place this project treats an unrun check as
success: exit 0 means "nothing was le

t through", and a check that did not run let
nothing through. SKIP is counted and listed separately

so the distinction survives
into the report, and `allSkipped` is reported so a caller is not left to

tinction survives
into the report, and `allSkipped` is reported so a caller is not left to infer it.
## `verify` checks both directions

`verify` runs a labelled corpus and reports two rates, because a verdict system can
fail in two ways
and only one is dangerous:

* **`lost` let through as `safe_to_compact`** — the dangerous one. Work is compacted
and gone. Exit

**1**.
* **`keep` refused** — the safe direction, and still a defect. A tool that always
answers `pr

eserve_first` never loses anything and is useless, so

## Requirements

Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`. No runtime dependencies. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is an
optional peer.
